title: The World Of The Unseen The Testimony Of Inspiration And The Summary Of The 14th And 15th Degrees

questions.question: What is the main belief statement expressed at the beginning of the target passage?
questions.answer: Allah alone is worthy of worship, and He necessarily exists as the One without partner.

questions.question: What are the two broad kinds of evidence named in the passage for Allah’s existence and oneness?
questions.answer: True revelations and truthful inspirations.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do true revelations include besides the basic message from Allah?
questions.answer: They include divine communication, Allah making Himself known, merciful answers to people’s prayers, and signs showing His existence to creation.

questions.question: What do truthful inspirations include, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They include signs of Allah’s love, answers to prayers, help for servants who seek aid, and inner indications of His existence.

questions.question: How do revelation and inspiration work together in the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: Both agree in pointing to the same truth, which strengthens the proof of Allah’s necessary existence and unity.

questions.question: Why is the repeated idea of agreement and consensus important in this passage?
questions.answer: It shows that many different forms of divine communication support one conclusion together, not separately or randomly.

questions.question: In this passage, what kind of relationship between Allah and His creatures is emphasized?
questions.answer: A caring relationship in which Allah communicates, responds, helps, and makes His presence known.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about people’s prayers and cries for help?
questions.answer: They are not ignored; Allah responds to them with mercy and support.

questions.question: How does the wording of the passage show that Allah’s communication reaches different creatures in different ways?
questions.answer: It mentions both revelation and inspiration, showing that divine communication is given through more than one form.

questions.question: What central conclusion should a reader draw from the whole passage?
questions.answer: All true divine messages and inspirations together testify that Allah exists necessarily and is absolutely one.

questions.question: In the opening summary, what lesson did the traveler gain from the unseen world?
questions.answer: He learned knowledge of Allah through the witness of revelation and true inspiration.

questions.question: Which attributes of Allah are directly highlighted in the statement of faith in this passage?
questions.answer: That He necessarily exists, is one, and is single in His unity.

questions.question: What does the passage teach through the phrase about all true revelations being in agreement?
questions.answer: That genuine revelations all support the same belief about Allah rather than contradicting one another.

questions.question: How are human prayers presented in connection with divine revelation?
questions.answer: Revelation includes Allah’s merciful response to people when they call on Him.

questions.question: What role do inspirations play in relation to Allah’s creatures?
questions.answer: They give loving, merciful, and supportive signs that make Allah’s existence known to them.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the passage’s mention of appeals for aid?
questions.answer: Allah is aware of human weakness and provides help to His servants.

questions.question: What idea about Allah’s mercy appears in both revelation and inspiration?
questions.answer: In both, Allah responds compassionately to those who turn to Him.

questions.question: If a student had to summarize this whole passage in one sentence, what would be a strong summary?
questions.answer: Every true form of divine communication, whether revelation or inspiration, points together to Allah’s certain existence and absolute oneness.

questions.question: What truth is being supported by the Arabic declaration and its English explanation in the passage?
questions.answer: That Allah alone is God and that His existence and unity are proven by revelation and true inspiration.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does revelation show about Allah’s way of dealing with humanity?
questions.answer: He speaks, makes Himself known, responds with mercy, and gives signs of His existence.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does truthful inspiration show about Allah’s dealings with creation?
questions.answer: He shows love, answers prayers, helps those who seek rescue, and gives awareness of His existence.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by presenting revelations as a “consensus” and inspirations as an “agreement”?
questions.answer: It means both groups give a united witness to the same reality about Allah.

questions.question: Is the argument in the passage based on one single event or on many signs taken together?
questions.answer: It is based on many signs gathered together.

questions.question: What kind of comprehension skill is needed to see why the passage lists many kinds of divine communication?
questions.answer: A reader needs to recognize that the list builds a cumulative argument, where each part adds force to the main claim.

questions.question: What can be inferred about Allah’s nearness from the mention of responses to prayers and cries for help?
questions.answer: Allah is not distant or unaware; He actively responds to His creation.

questions.question: How does the passage balance Allah’s greatness with His care for creation?
questions.answer: It presents Him as the One true God while also showing that He lovingly answers, helps, and makes Himself known.

questions.question: What misunderstanding would this passage correct for someone who thinks divine guidance is random or disconnected?
questions.answer: It would correct that by showing that genuine revelation and inspiration are consistent and united in one message.

questions.question: What is the strongest overall proof pattern used in this passage?
questions.answer: Repeated and unified testimony from many true divine signs leading to one conclusion about Allah.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly trying to prove?
questions.answer: It is trying to prove Allah’s necessary existence and His oneness.

questions.question: What source of proof is mentioned first in the passage?
questions.answer: All true revelations.

questions.question: What source of proof is mentioned after that?
questions.answer: All truthful inspirations.

questions.question: What are some examples of what true revelations contain in this passage?
questions.answer: They contain divine communication, Allah’s self-disclosure, merciful answers to prayer, and signs of His existence.

questions.question: What are some examples of what truthful inspirations contain?
questions.answer: They contain divine love, answers to prayers, help for those asking for aid, and signs of Allah’s existence.

questions.question: How does the passage connect belief in Allah with lived human experience?
questions.answer: It ties belief to prayer, calling for help, receiving mercy, and becoming aware of Allah’s presence.

questions.question: Why does the passage repeatedly speak about Allah responding?
questions.answer: To show that His relation to creation includes action, mercy, and communication, not only power.

questions.question: What can we infer about the value of sincere prayer from this passage?
questions.answer: Sincere prayer matters because Allah responds to His creatures and servants.

questions.question: How would you compare revelation and inspiration based on this passage alone?
questions.answer: Both are forms of divine communication, but revelation is presented more publicly and comprehensively, while inspiration is described more personally and inwardly.

questions.question: What final idea ties all parts of the passage together?
questions.answer: Every true sign from Allah, whether through revelation or inspiration, leads to recognizing Him as the only true God.

questions.question: In this passage, what does the phrase about “no god but Allah” lead into?
questions.answer: It leads into an explanation of the proofs for Allah’s existence and unity.

questions.question: What does the passage say true revelations testify to?
questions.answer: They testify that Allah necessarily exists and is one.

questions.question: What does the passage say truthful inspirations testify to?
questions.answer: They also testify that Allah necessarily exists and is one.

questions.question: How does the passage show that Allah is merciful?
questions.answer: It says He responds compassionately to the prayers of His creatures.

questions.question: How does the passage show that Allah is loving?
questions.answer: It says true inspirations contain expressions of His love.

questions.question: What does the mention of aid and appeals for help add to the meaning of the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that Allah supports His servants when they are in need.

questions.question: What idea about knowledge of Allah comes from this passage?
questions.answer: People can know Allah through the truthful signs of His communication and response.

questions.question: If someone asked whether the passage presents Allah as silent toward creation, what would the best answer be?
questions.answer: No; it presents Him as communicating, responding, helping, and making His existence known.

questions.question: What is a good thematic title for this passage?
questions.answer: The united witness of revelation and inspiration to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What core Islamic belief is affirmed in the first line of the target passage?
questions.answer: The belief that only Allah is God and that He exists necessarily as the One.

questions.question: How is revelation described as supporting faith in Allah?
questions.answer: It gives a united testimony through divine messages, self-disclosure, merciful answers, and signs of His existence.

questions.question: How is inspiration described as supporting faith in Allah?
questions.answer: It gives a united testimony through love, answered prayers, help in times of need, and inner signs of His existence.

questions.question: What do the repeated references to Allah’s responses teach about dua?
questions.answer: They teach that calling on Allah is meaningful because He answers and cares for His creation.

questions.question: What effect does the structure of the passage have on the reader?
questions.answer: It builds confidence by stacking one form of evidence after another toward the same conclusion.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the truthfulness of divine guidance from the passage?
questions.answer: True divine guidance is consistent and never points away from Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: How does this passage help a believer think about moments of weakness or need?
questions.answer: It reminds the believer that Allah hears, responds, and provides support.

questions.question: In what way is this passage both theological and personal?
questions.answer: It teaches a doctrine about Allah’s existence and unity while also showing His loving and merciful care in real human need.

questions.question: Why would the agreement of many revelations and inspirations be stronger than a single claim?
questions.answer: Because many truthful witnesses supporting the same point make the conclusion firmer and more convincing.

questions.question: What is the best overall conclusion from the target passage?
questions.answer: The full range of true divine communication bears one united witness that Allah alone is the necessarily existing and absolutely one Lord.
